question: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
solution:
**Given:**

George can do 35% of the total work = 6 days

(Jim + George) can do the same work = 12 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

George can do 35% of the total work = 6 days

George can do 100% of the total work = (6 × 100)/35 days

⇒ (6 × 20)/7 = 120/7 days

Efficiency of Jim + George = 10 units/day

⇒ Jim + 7 = 10 

⇒ Efficiency of Jim = 10 - 7 = 3

Total time taken to do the entire work = 120/3 = 40 days

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**
